text: Carla Hall, born on May 12, 1964, is an American chef, television personality, and former model who was born and raised in Nashville, Tennessee. She graduated from Hillsboro High School and earned a degree in accounting from Howard University's Business School in 1986. After working as a Certified Public Accountant at Price Waterhouse in Tampa, Florida for two years, she left due to disliking the job. She then worked as a model on the runways of Paris, Milan, and London, during which time she decided to pursue a culinary career. Upon returning to the United States, she moved to Washington, D.C., where she started a lunch delivery service called the Lunch Bunch after her friend's coworkers expressed interest in her leftover sandwiches. After four years, she enrolled at L'Academie de Cuisine in Bethesda, Maryland, earning a Culinary Career Training certificate and later completing an externship at the Henley Park Hotel, where she was promoted to sous chef. By 1999, she became the executive chef at the Garden Cafe in the State Plaza Hotel and later served as executive chef at the Washington Club. In 2001, she founded Alchemy Caterers in Wheaton, Maryland, which she later renamed Alchemy by Carla Hall, and she remains in charge of the company. She authored the cookbook Cooking with Love: Comfort Food that Hugs You. Her big break came in 2008 when she competed on Top Chef: New York, where her crawfish gumbo earned her top-rated dish in the Thanksgiving challenge and Super Bowl XLIII tickets; she won two more challenges and was in the top for several others, impressing judges Jacques Pépin and Emeril Lagasse. She finished as runner-up to Hosea Rosenberg in the final challenge of the season. Hall gained popularity on the show for her personality and her call-and-response phrase "Hootie Hoo!", which she and her husband used to locate each other. She promoted the philosophy of "cooking with love," stating that cooking with care and calmness results in better food, and if one is not in a good mood, the only thing to make is a reservation. She participated in Top Chef: All-Stars, the eighth season, where she finished fifth overall and was awarded "Fan Favorite" by viewers, beating out Fabio Viviani. Since September 26, 2011, she has been one of the five co-hosts on The Chew, a one-hour ABC show centered on food from all angles that replaced All My Children, and remained a cohost until its cancellation in 2018. In 2014, she launched a Kickstarter campaign that raised $264,703 from 1,550 backers, exceeding her $250,000 goal, to open her restaurant Carla Hall's Southern Kitchen, which opened on June 17, 2016, in Brooklyn, New York, and closed in August 2017. She appeared on the May 3, 2009, cover of the Washington Post Magazine in a feature titled "Fit for Fame" about exercising while being famous. She portrayed a version of herself named "Spaghetti Scientist Carla Hall" in the BoJack Horseman episode "That Went Well," voiced Mpishi the harrier hawk in a season 2 episode of The Lion Guard titled "Ono and the Egg," and voiced the president in Season 1, Episode 5 of Butterbean's Café titled "A Grilled Cheese for the Big Cheese!" In 2016, she made a cameo in Fox's The Passion: New Orleans as a food truck operator. In 2018, she made a guest appearance on ABC's General Hospital as the Quartermaine family's cook. She has served as a judge on Food Network's Halloween Baking Championship and, in 2020, also hosted the season. She appeared as a judge on Season 7 of Food Network's Holiday Baking Championship as a replacement for Lorraine Pascal due to COVID-19 restrictions. In 2020, she judged the Channel 4 competition series Crazy Delicious, which took place on an edible set and was hosted by Jayde Adams alongside Heston Blumenthal and Niklas Ekstedt. As of 2020, she is featured in segments with Sesame Street characters Cookie Monster and Gonger in Snack Chat. In 2021, she appeared in Antiques Roadshow Celebrity Edition, episode 2, hosted Worst Cooks in America with Anne Burrell, and is a host and judge on Best Baker in America. In 2022, she was the headliner judge for the National Gingerbread House Competition. Hall lives in Washington, D.C. and married Matthew Lyons in 2006; she has a stepson named Noah.
